---
name: dreamers-update
description: 'Maintain Dreamers shared sources and validate both Copilot and Codex packages in one repository. Triggers: /dreamers-update.'
argument-hint: '<what to change>'
---

Follow YAGNI principles when writing or planning code.

$ARGUMENTS

Follow the Dreamers Kernel and output discipline from `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`.
If no task description was provided, halt and ask via `request_information`.

## Scope

This repository owns both runtime packages. Keep the canonical Copilot layout under `.github/`: skills, Markdown agents, refs, templates, instructions, and `catalog.json`. Preserve catalog paths and collections so catalog installation continues to work. Do not maintain or transfer changes into a separate Codex repository.

Codex output is generated by `scripts/build-codex.py`. Edit shared behavior in `.github/`; edit only runtime differences in `adapters/codex/`. Never hand-edit generated skills or TOML agents. The converter must reject unsupported runtime tokens and adapter drift before installation.

## Workflow

1. Apply the Dreamers Kernel and `git-workflow`. Create one feature branch from the current remote default branch, preserving unrelated work.
2. Apply the requested source change. Update affected READMEs and catalog descriptions without relocating catalog targets. Keep behavior shared; use Codex adapters only for input, tool, agent format, resource resolution, and instruction loading differences.
3. Synchronize refs with `scripts/sync-refs.sh -Sync` on Bash or `scripts/sync-refs.ps1 -Sync` on PowerShell. Run the matching `Test-DreamersCopilot` and `Test-DreamersCodex` scripts. Both targets must pass before close-out. Run tests for changed build/install behavior too.
4. Use `/dreamers-review` for artifact-backed review; apply findings and revalidate. Use `/dreamers-docs` for affected documentation.
5. Commit explicit paths with a conventional subject and `Co-authored-by: The Dreamers System`. Present the tested scope and ask for final PR approval. Approval already given for the current action satisfies its gate. On approval use `/dreamers-pr` for one push and one PR covering both targets.
6. Refresh the existing local Codex installation from the validated source checkout, including this skill. Follow the installation requirements below. Do not change consuming project repositories or archive/delete the former Codex repository automatically.

## Local Codex installation

- Resolve the target from `CODEX_HOME`, falling back to `~/.codex`. State the resolved destination before writing. Refreshing an existing Dreamers installation is included; obtain any environment-required permission before creating a new installation.
- Before overwriting, back up existing Dreamers-managed destination files outside the install target, preferably in this repo's ignored `.dreamers/backups/` with a timestamp. Preserve unrelated skills, configuration, credentials, and user files.
- Run `bash ./Install-DreamersCodex.sh --force --codex-home "$target"` on Bash, or `./Install-DreamersCodex.ps1 -Force -CodexHome $target` on PowerShell. The installers generate and validate Codex files from this checkout before copying them. Force is required to refresh existing files.
- Generate a fresh package using `python3 scripts/build-codex.py --output <empty-directory>` (use `python` where appropriate). Verify installed skills, TOML agents, refs, templates, and instructions byte-for-byte against that generated package. Verify the managed Dreamers block in the global `AGENTS.md` against the generated `AGENTS.md` fragment, preserving personal text outside its markers. Confirm the installed `dreamers-update/SKILL.md` includes this installation step. An installer exit code alone is insufficient.
- Report source commit, destination, backup location, and byte verification. A failed install or verification leaves the update incomplete. Start a new Codex session to load refreshed skills and agents.

## Exit

Report changed shared sources and adapters, catalog compatibility, both validations, review status, PR URL when created, and local installation/backup/verification results. Report concrete blockers without claiming completion.
